mainTopic: Whose agents כהנים are, whether a קרבן needs the owner's awareness, and then the next line of the משנה, about separating תרומה.
overview: The גמרא is trying to decide whether a כהן offering a קרבן acts for Heaven (שלוחי דשמיא) or for the owner (שלוחי דידן). A ברייתא seems to let a כהן offer a full חטאת and אשם for someone he forbade to benefit from him. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the קרבנות of a מצורע, which even a child brings, so they need no awareness from the owner. Next, a משנה says a כהן who makes a קרבן פיגול by mistake still makes it truly פיגול, which suggests the כהן is Heaven's agent. The גמרא rejects that proof because the פסוק 'לא יחשב לו' makes פיגול count in any case. Then the גמרא goes back (גופא) to רבי יוחנן's rule that every קרבן needs the owner's awareness except a מחוסר כפרה. It answers two challenges to that rule: the case of a שוטה wife cannot involve a חטאת for חלב, and including young children in a father's פסח is not a Torah law. A משנה and a ברייתא show that a father's 'first to ירושלים' promise is only meant to make his children eager for מצוות. Finally, the גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about separating תרומה.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets a כהן offer a sin-offering and guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אבא challenges using a ברייתא: a כהן who forbade someone from benefiting from him may still sprinkle that person's חטאת and אשם blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אבא raised an objection: If the person was a כהן, he may sprinkle the blood of the other person's sin-offering and guilt-offering for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אבא quotes a ברייתא that seems to let the כהן do even the bigger, more personal קרבנות for the person forbidden to benefit from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת and an אשם normally need the owner's knowledge and intent. If the כהן may still offer them for someone he is not allowed to help, it sounds like he is not doing the person a favor at all. He is just working for Heaven, so this seems to show that כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection from a source
he will sprinkle (the blood on the מזבח)
sin-offering
guilt-offering
someone forbidden by a נדר to benefit from another person

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Abba raised an objection:
If he was a kohen,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person who made the נדר forbidding the other person to benefit from him.

phrases.english: he may sprinkle for him the blood of his sin-offering
and the blood of his guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא or שלוחי דידן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a כהן who made a נדר forbidding someone to benefit from him may offer for that person only קרבנות that do not need the owner's knowledge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת and an אשם need the owner's knowledge, yet the כהן may offer them. That implies the כהן is not acting for the owner but for Heaven.

steps.title: It means the offerings of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the חטאת and אשם of a מצורע. Even a child brings these, so they do not need the owner's understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the blood of a מצורע's sin-offering and a מצורע's guilt-offering, as it is written: 'This shall be the law of the מצורע,' meaning both an adult and a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the ברייתא so that it talks only about the special קרבנות of a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's word תורת teaches that one law covers every מצורע, even a קטן who has no legal understanding. So these קרבנות work without the owner's knowledge, just like the other קרבנות the כהן was already allowed to offer. That means the ברייתא proves nothing about whose agent the כהן is.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with צרעת who brings קרבנות to finish becoming טהור
the law of; one rule covering every case
both an adult and a minor

phrases.english: The blood of the sin-offering of a metzora
and the blood of the guilt-offering of a metzora.
As it is written: "This shall be the law of the metzora,"
whether an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי בר אבא's objection by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a מצורע's קרבנות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means any חטאת and אשם, including ones that need the owner's knowledge.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only a מצורע's קרבנות, which work without the owner's knowledge because even a קטן brings them.

steps.title: The משנה about כהנים who made a קרבן פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: כהנים who made a קרבן פיגול on purpose must pay. The גמרא reads into it that if they did it by mistake they do not pay, but the קרבן is still פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: כהנים who made a קרבן פיגול in the מקדש on purpose are liable. This implies that if they did it by mistake they are exempt, but the פיגול they caused is still פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source and draws a detail out of it. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states the case of doing it on purpose. From that, the גמרא reads that doing it by mistake brings no payment. Either way, the כהן's wrong intention really does ruin the קרבן, and that is the detail the next step will use.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned in a משנה
made a קרבן פיגול by intending to eat it after its proper time
acting on purpose
acting by mistake
this implies (reading the opposite case out of the words)

phrases.english: We learned: Priests who caused piggul in the Temple,
phrases.notes: פיגול means they did the עבודה while planning to eat the קרבן after its allowed time.

phrases.english: if on purpose, they are liable.
phrases.notes: Liable to pay the owner for the קרבן they ruined.

phrases.english: This implies: if by mistake, they are exempt,
but their piggul is piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was pushed aside, the גמרא tries a new source to settle the question.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about כהנים who made a קרבן פיגול

steps.title: An owner's agent could not ruin the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא, it makes sense that their פיגול counts. If they were our agents, the owner could say: I sent you to fix things, not to ruin them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they are agents of Heaven; that is why their פיגול is פיגול. But if you say they are our agents, why is their פיגול פיגול? Let the owner say to him: I made you my agent to do things right, not to ruin them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה to argue that כהנים must be שלוחי דשמיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that an agent who acts against the sender's interest has acted outside his agency. If the כהן were the owner's agent, his ruining the קרבן should not count, and it should not become פיגול. Since the משנה says it does become פיגול, the כהן must be acting for Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well if you say
agents of Heaven
our agents (agents of the owner)
to fix things, not to ruin them

steps.whatToRemember: An agent sent by a person cannot ruin things for that person: 'שליחא שויתיך לתקוני ולא לעוותי'. This proof tries to show that כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא, but the next step rejects it.
steps.confusionAlert: Even if כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא, the owner still brings and owns the קרבן. The question is only whose agent the כהן is while he does the עבודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whose agent the כהן is affects whether a כהן may serve for someone forbidden to benefit from him.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
they are agents of Heaven,
that is why their piggul is piggul.
But if you say
they are our agents,
why is their piggul piggul?
Let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The owner of the קרבן is the one speaking to the כהן.

phrases.english: I made you an agent to fix things
and not to ruin them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא שְׁלוּחֵי דִשְׁמַיָּא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the detail drawn out in step 3 (פיגול by mistake still counts) to build the proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that a כהן's פיגול counts, together with the agency rule 'לתקוני ולא לעוותי'

steps.title: פיגול is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof from פיגול is rejected. The פסוק 'לא יחשב לו' teaches that פיגול works no matter what, so it tells us nothing about whose agents the כהנים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: פיגול is different, because the פסוק says 'it will not be counted for him,' which means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Steps 3-4. פיגול has its own special rule from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 argued that a כהן's mistaken פיגול counts only if he is Heaven's agent. Here the גמרא says the פסוק makes פיגול take effect 'מכל מקום', in any case, even if the owner would object. So פיגול proves nothing about the nature of the כהנים' agency.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They say', the scholars answering the proof
It is different
'It will not be counted for him', the פסוק about פיגול
In any case, no matter what

steps.whatToRemember: The question of שלוחי דשמיא versus שלוחי דידן is still not proven. פיגול is a special rule that comes from a פסוק.

phrases.english: They say: It is different regarding פיגול,
for the verse says, "it will not be counted for him,"
meaning: in any case.
phrases.notes: So even if the owner never agreed to it, the פיגול still counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Steps 3-4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from a כהן's mistaken פיגול about the כהנים' status as agents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פיגול takes effect because of a special פסוק, not because of agency law.

steps.title: Every קרבן needs the owner's awareness, except a מחוסר כפרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that every קרבן needs the owner's awareness except for a מחוסר כפרה. His proof is that a father brings a קרבן for his young children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main statement: רבי יוחנן said: everyone needs awareness except someone lacking atonement, since a person brings a קרבן for his young sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back (גופא) to examine רבי יוחנן's rule, which was mentioned earlier. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a קרבן needs the owner's awareness and agreement. A מחוסר כפרה is different, because someone can bring his קרבן for him. We know this because young children cannot understand anything, yet their father brings their קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself', going back to look closely at a statement quoted earlier
Need awareness or agreement of the owner
Someone still missing a קרבן to finish his purification, such as a מצורע
Young children

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone needs awareness,
except one who is lacking atonement,
for a person brings an offering
for his young sons and daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns (גופא) to רבי יוחנן's statement quoted earlier in the sugya to examine it on its own. His rule stands behind the answer in Step 2, that a מצורע's קרבנות need no awareness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every קרבן needs the owner's awareness except the קרבן of a מחוסר כפרה.

steps.title: Then could one bring a חטאת for a friend's חלב?
steps.stepSummary: If someone can bring a קרבן without the owner's awareness, a person should be able to bring a חטאת for a friend who ate חלב. A husband does bring for his שוטה wife, according to רבי יהודה. But רבי אלעזר says that doing this for a friend accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, let a person bring a חטאת for חלב on behalf of his friend, just as a person brings for his insane wife, according to רבי יהודה. So why did רבי אלעזר say that one who set aside a חטאת for חלב for his friend did nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. The case of the שוטה wife seems to show that a person can bring a חטאת for someone else, but רבי אלעזר says you cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge compares two cases. A husband brings a קרבן for his wife who is a שוטה and has no awareness. That suggests a חטאת does not need the owner's awareness. So a חטאת for a friend's חלב should also work, yet רבי אלעזר rules it is worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so', drawing a strange result from a rule
A חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake
A woman who is mentally incompetent
Why then?

phrases.english: But if so,

phrases.aramaic: יָבִיא אָדָם חַטַּאת חֵלֶב עַל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: let a person bring a sin-offering for forbidden fat on behalf of his friend,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אָדָם מֵבִיא עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ שׁוֹטָה,
phrases.english: just as a person brings an offering for his insane wife,
according to Rabbi Yehuda.
Why then did Rabbi Elazar say:
If one set aside a sin-offering for forbidden fat on behalf of his friend,
he did nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה יָבִיא אָדָם חַטַּאת חֵלֶב עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a קרבן can be brought without the owner's awareness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שוטה wife case seems to allow a חטאת without awareness. That conflicts with רבי אלעזר's ruling that a חטאת for a friend's חלב is worthless.

steps.title: If she ate while she was a שוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of the שוטה wife really is. If she ate חלב while she was a שוטה, she is not obligated in a קרבן at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The insane wife, what is the case? If she ate it while insane, she is not obligated in a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer by asking what the wife's case actually looks like. It checks the first possibility here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה is not responsible for her actions. So חלב eaten while she was a שוטה creates no חטאת obligation. That means the husband's קרבן cannot be a חטאת for this חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Someone obligated to bring a קרבן

phrases.english: His insane wife, what is the case?
If she ate the fat while she was insane,
she is not someone obligated in an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of Step 7 by questioning the case it was built on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes apart the comparison by defining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband brings a חטאת for his שוטה wife's חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: If she ate while insane, there is no חטאת obligation at all.

steps.title: If she ate while sane and then became a שוטה
steps.stepSummary: If she ate while she was sane and then became a שוטה, her קרבן is disqualified. רבי יוחנן rules that a קרבן pushed off by insanity stays pushed off. So the wife's case cannot be a חטאת for חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she ate while sane and then became insane: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן that if one ate חלב, set aside a קרבן, became insane, and became sane again, the קרבן is disqualified. Since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the second possibility and finishes its answer. Neither case allows a חטאת for חלב, so the comparison to a friend's חלב falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a person who was obligated loses his חטאת once he becomes a שוטה, because the קרבן is נדחה and stays rejected. So the husband's קרבן for his שוטה wife must be some other kind of קרבן, not a חטאת for חלב. That means it gives no proof about bringing a חטאת for a friend.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentally competent, sane
Became sane again
Since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off for good

steps.whatToRemember: The שוטה wife case cannot be a חטאת for חלב. So it does not prove that one may bring a חטאת for a friend, and רבי אלעזר's ruling and רבי יוחנן's rule do not clash.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though she later becomes sane, the קרבן does not come back. Once it was pushed off, it is disqualified forever.

phrases.english: And if she ate it while sane and then became insane,
but Rabbi Yirmeya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and became insane, and then became sane again,
the offering is disqualified,
since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer begun in Step 8 by ruling out the second possibility.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes apart the comparison by ruling out both possible cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps she ate while sane, so the husband brings her חטאת for חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once she became a שוטה, her חטאת was pushed off forever. So the husband's קרבן is not a חטאת for חלב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It protects both רבי יוחנן's rule about a מחוסר כפרה and רבי אלעזר's ruling that one cannot bring a חטאת for a friend.

steps.title: Why can't a person bring a פסח for a friend?
steps.stepSummary: A father brings a פסח for his young children without their awareness. So a person should be able to bring a פסח for a friend. Yet רבי אלעזר says that doing this accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a person should be able to bring a פסח for his friend, since a person brings one for his young sons and daughters. Why then did רבי אלעזר say that someone who set aside a פסח for his friend did nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge, this time from קרבן פסח. A father brings a פסח for his young children without asking them, so why can't someone do the same for a friend?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier challenge was about a חטאת, and it was answered. Now the גמרא tries the same kind of attack with a different קרבן. If a father's פסח covers his children without their awareness, awareness should not be needed for a friend either, yet רבי אלעזר rules that such a פסח does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if that is so (opens a challenge built on what was just said)
The Paschal lamb offering
Set aside (an animal for a קרבן)
He has done nothing; it does not work

phrases.english: But now, if that is so,
let a person bring a Paschal offering for his friend,
since a person brings one
for his young sons and daughters.
Why then did רבי אלעזר say:
one who set aside a Paschal offering for his friend
has done nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה יָבִיא אָדָם פֶּסַח עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חטאת challenge is answered, the גמרא raises a parallel challenge from קרבן פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a קרבן can be brought for someone without his awareness, as shown by a father bringing for his young children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father brings a פסח for his children without their awareness. So a friend should also be able to bring one for another person, but רבי אלעזר says that does nothing.

steps.title: Including children in the father's פסח is not a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the rule of 'a lamb for each father's house' does not come from the Torah. So the father's case teaches nothing about bringing for a friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: 'A lamb for each father's house' is not a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. Including young children in the father's פסח is not a Torah-level rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the father's פסח truly counts for his children by Torah law. רבי זירא says it does not. So there is no proof that a קרבן פסח can work for someone without his awareness, and רבי אלעזר's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb for each father's house (שמות 12:3)
Not from the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא does not say a father stops bringing for his children. He only says this practice is not required by Torah law.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:
"A lamb for each father's house"
is not from the Torah.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes away the basis of the comparison: the father's case is not Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A father's פסח counts for his young children by Torah law, which would show that awareness is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Including the children is not a Torah law, so it proves nothing about bringing a פסח for a friend.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: ״שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבֹת״ לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא

steps.title: Proof from the father who promises the פסח to the first child to reach ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the first child to reach ירושלים adds his brothers to the פסח after it was already slaughtered. That would be impossible if the children's share were a Torah law, since no one can join a פסח after its slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this? From a משנה: If a father says to his sons, 'I am slaughtering the פסח for whichever of you reaches ירושלים first,' then once the first one brings in his head and most of his body, he gets his share and gives his brothers a share with him. If 'a lamb for the household' were a Torah law, how could he stand over meat that is already slaughtered and give them a share?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי זירא's claim from a משנה about a father, his sons, and a race to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, people must join a פסח before it is slaughtered. In the משנה, the first son adds his brothers after the slaughter, and it still works. That only makes sense if the children's share is not a real Torah requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know this?
His head and most of his body
He acquired his share
Gives someone else a share

phrases.english: And from where do we know this?
From what we learned in a משנה:
One who says to his sons:
I am slaughtering the Paschal offering
for whichever of you goes up
first to Jerusalem,
once the first one has brought in
his head and most of his body,
he acquires his share,
and gives his brothers a share along with him.
And if you say
"a lamb for the household" is from the Torah,
he is standing over the meat,
phrases.notes: By the time he arrives, the פסח is already slaughtered, and by Torah law no one can join it after that.

phrases.english: and he gives them a share?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי זירא's answer in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that including children in the father's פסח is not Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a father who slaughters the פסח for whichever son reaches ירושלים first.

steps.title: Then why does the father make the promise?
steps.stepSummary: If the children's share is not a real Torah requirement, why does the father bother promising the פסח to the first one who arrives?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do they need their father to say this to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the משנה. If no real acquiring happens, what is the point of the father's statement? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 12 showed that the children's share is not a Torah requirement. That makes the father's promise look pointless, so the גמרא asks why he says it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do they need it?
Their father

phrases.english: But why do they need
that their father says this to them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the father's words in the משנה just cited.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the father's promise if it does not create a real Torah-level share?

steps.title: The promise makes the children eager to do מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The father makes the promise to get his children excited about doing מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make them eager in doing מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The father's promise is a way to motivate the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The race to ירושלים is not a legal act of acquiring. It is חינוך, a way to get the children moving quickly and happily toward the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To make them eager and quick
Commandments

phrases.english: In order to make them eager in doing מצוות.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's statement is meant to motivate the children, not to create a legal share.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the daughters beat the sons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a race in which the daughters arrived first. It concludes only that the daughters were eager and the sons were lazy. This shows the race was about motivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: There was an incident where the daughters got there before the sons, and the daughters were found to be eager and the sons lazy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the answer of step 14 with a ברייתא about a real case where this race happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's lesson is about who was eager and who was lazy, not about who acquired the meat. That fits the idea that the father's promise was only meant to motivate the children.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (introduces support)
There was an incident
Eager, quick (feminine)
Lazy, sluggish

steps.whatToRemember: Including young children in the father's פסח is not a Torah law, so it cannot prove that a קרבן works without the owner's awareness. The father's 'first to ירושלים' promise is חינוך, a way to make the children eager for מצוות.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא:
There was an incident
and the daughters got there before the sons,
and the daughters were found to be eager
and the sons lazy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the answer of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the father's promise is only meant to motivate the children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an incident in which the daughters beat the sons and were praised as eager.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה about separating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה. It says a person may separate תרומה for someone who is forbidden by a vow to benefit from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'And he separates his תרומה,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss that line in the next steps. This is a setup step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists tasks a person may do for a מודר הנאה, even though the vow forbids that person to get any benefit from him. Separating someone's תרומה looks like it could be a benefit to him. That is why the גמרא is about to look at this line closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates תרומה, setting aside the כהן's portion from produce
The portion of produce that must be given to a כהן
Short for 'and so on.' It means the rest of the quoted line continues
Someone who is forbidden by a vow to get benefit from another person

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling from the גמרא. It is only a quote from the משנה. The real discussion starts in the next step.

phrases.english: And he separates his תרומה, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion (steps 6 to 15, testing רבי יוחנן's rule that every קרבן needs the owner's awareness except a מחוסר כפרה) has ended. The גמרא now moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person who made the vow may separate תרומה from the produce of the person forbidden to benefit from him.
